title: Social Sciences · Seq 1 Humanities and social sciences

questions.stem: According to the introduction, humanities and social sciences:
options: Are both focused on human life
Differ in that humanities are mostly analytical or philosophical
Differ in that social sciences are more scientific and experimental
Are both classified as natural sciences
questions.explanation: Humanities are classified as non-science academic disciplines.

questions.stem: About the history of the humanities:
options: They are traditionally known as the liberal arts
Their modern conception dates from the Sophists in the mid-5th century BCE
They appeared with the Industrial Revolution
They date back to the ancient Greeks, who used them to educate citizens
questions.explanation: The Sophists' general education prepared young men for active citizenship in the polis (city-state).

questions.stem: Which disciplines belong to the humanities according to the course?
options: Literature and languages
Religion and history
Philosophy
Sociology
questions.explanation: Sociology is a social science (man as a social being). Humanities: history, philosophy, religion, languages, literatures, arts, media, cultural studies.

questions.stem: The Encyclopedia Britannica (2006) defines the humanities as:
options: Sciences dealing with the individual as a member of the group
General term for all sciences concerned with human affairs
The scientific study of social, cultural and economic forces
Branches of knowledge that investigate human beings, their culture and their self-expression
questions.explanation: B is the course's definition of social science; C is Fairchild's; D is Seligman's.

questions.stem: Characteristics of the humanities stated in the course:
options: They use narrative imagination as an important tool
Their methods are creative and speculative by nature
There is no search for objective truth
They explain the causality of events
questions.explanation: "It neither seeks objective truth nor tries to explain the causality of events."

questions.stem: What distinguishes the humanities from the natural sciences, according to the course?
options: The search for objective, measurable truth
The use of laboratory experiments
Their recent origin
The mode of approach to any question
questions.explanation: "What distinguishes the humanities from the natural Sciences is the mode of approach to any question."

questions.stem: The humanities are described as self-reflexive and answer the fundamental question:
options: How to measure human behaviour
What laws govern society
What it means to be human
How to cure social problems
questions.explanation: "…answers the fundamental question what it means to be human."

questions.stem: Compared with the humanities, the social sciences:
options: Study issues in a systematic and scientific way
Deal with the basic elements of culture that determine general patterns of human behaviour
Are more objective, relying on facts, experiments and reality
Are more subjective, relying on feelings and assumptions
questions.explanation: Subjectivity (experience, feelings, assumptions, philosophy) characterizes the humanities.

questions.stem: The humanities, unlike the social sciences:
options: Are more subjective
Express spiritual and aesthetic values and the meaning of life
Focus more on emotions and feelings than on the system employed
Rely mainly on experiments
questions.explanation: Reliance on facts and experiments is the social-science side of the comparison.

options: Studying how people interact, behave and develop a culture
Understanding all aspects of society
Studying only artistic self-expression
Finding solutions to deal with social problems
questions.explanation: Artistic self-expression is the domain of the humanities.

questions.stem: Match the scholar to his definition of social sciences:
options: Peter Lewis — concerned with the laws that govern society
Mitchell — the study of human self-expression through the arts
Fairchild — a general term for all the sciences concerned with human affairs
Seligman — sciences dealing with the activities of the individual as member of the group
questions.explanation: Mitchell: strictly, the application of the scientific method to the complex network of human relationships.

questions.stem: The social sciences view man from two dimensions. Which pairings are correct?
options: Man as an individual being — psychology
Man as a social being — philosophy
Man as a social being — sociology
Man as an individual being — sociology
questions.explanation: Individual: his way of thinking (psychology). Social: his behaviour with others (sociology).

questions.stem: According to the course, foreign-language learning develops at the same time:
options: Only grammatical accuracy
Social competence
Linguistic competence
Cognitive competence
questions.explanation: "Learners develop cognitive, social and linguistic competence at the same time."

questions.stem: Fields said to be natural byproducts of social-science thinking:
options: Literature
International relations
Law
Government
questions.explanation: Social-science thinking underlies law, international relations and government.

options: The first international medium used to interact with people worldwide
Needed for digital and internet communication and the professional world
Important in the world of education
Useful only for direct conversation
questions.explanation: English is "not only important in communicating directly" but also in education, technology and work, and for studying abroad.
